step8.importFromCanvasTip: Import the sections drawn on the canvas: lengths computed automatically from coordinates + scale, topology inferred from connections
step8.overrideHint: Columns 2–9 are editable (Excel-style cells). Leave a cell empty to revert to the calculated value; highlighted cells hold manually entered values.
step8.noSections: No sections defined. Add sections to size the network.
step8.noCanvasSections: No sections drawn in the diagram. Draw the network on the canvas first.
step8.allOk: ✓ All verified nodes satisfy H_B_min = {{hb}} mH₂O
step8.colQiTip: Flow entering the section: Qi = Qf + q_own (q_own = q_lin × L)
step8.colQfTip: Flow leaving the section: Qf = Q_ext + Qie + Σ Qi of child sections
step8.colQieTip: Hydrant flow, if the section feeds a hydrant
step8.colDiStasTip: Standardized inner diameter, chosen from the PEHD PN10 table based on Dp
step8.colDeStasTip: Standardized outer diameter, matching Di STAS in the PEHD PN10 table
step8.colVefTip: Effective velocity, recomputed from the continuity equation for the standardized diameter
step8.colReTip: Reynolds number: Re = Vef × Di STAS / ν
step8.colDOverKTip: Threshold used to determine the flow regime, based on the diameter/roughness ratio
step8.colLambdaTip: Friction coefficient (Darcy-Weisbach), computed based on the flow regime
step8.colRegimTip: Flow regime from Re and 23·D/k: laminar, smooth turbulent, transitional or rough turbulent
step8.colHrTip: Total head loss on the section: hr = h_lin + h_loc (h_lin = ih × L, h_loc = ζ × Vef²/(2×9.81))
step8.colHnecTip: Minimum required pressure at the consumer (Hb from Step 7 — Reservoir)
step8.colHPiezDownTip: Downstream piezometric elevation: upstream piezo elevation − hr
step8.colCotaDownValTip: Ground (topographic) elevation at the downstream end of the section
step8.colPressureDownTip: Available pressure at the downstream end: Hd = Piezo. elev. − Ground elev.
step8.colPressureDownBarTip: Available pressure converted to bar: Hd [mH₂O] / 10.2

terrain.fetchFailed: Terrain elevations could not be retrieved
terrain.autoToggleTip: Fills the upstream/downstream ground elevation of each section from the digital elevation model (SRTM ~30 m, ±2–5 m). Manually entered elevations are never changed.
terrain.demTip: Estimated from the terrain model (±2–5 m) — verify against the topographic survey.
terrain.resetToDemTip: Discard the manual value and use the terrain model elevation
terrain.needsAnchor: Anchor the map (🗺 Map) to get automatic terrain elevations.
terrain.topoTip: Elevation taken from the imported survey points.

topo.title: Survey points
topo.intro: Import measured elevations (topographic survey, GPS). A point within the given radius of a section end sets its elevation, taking priority over the DEM; in 3D the terrain is locally corrected to pass through the points.
topo.crsStereo70: Stereo 70 — X = North, Y = East (survey convention)
topo.formats: CSV/TXT: [Name] X Y Z (separator ; , tab or space) · GPX · KML (altitudeMode “absolute” only)
topo.radiusTip: Maximum distance [m] between a survey point and a section end for the point to set its elevation
topo.nothingImported: No points with elevation in the file
topo.readFailed: The file could not be read
topo.resultNoZKml: Without real elevation (skipped): {{n}} — Google Earth KML is usually “clampToGround”, without elevations
topo.none: No survey points in the project.
topo.needsAnchor: Anchor the map (🗺 Map) so the points can be placed on the plan.
